To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the prevalence of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease is 20-30% in the general population and is associated with obesity, insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome; (2) the prevalence of NAFLD is higher in men than in women; (3) NAFLD is more prevalent in Hispanics and African Americans than in non-Hispanic whites, but the reasons for this are not clear; (4) NAFLD increases the risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease
the presence of steatosis in the setting of hemochromatotic liver injury is associated with increased fibrosis.

1) a significant proportion of HCC patients have NAFLD, 2) NAFLD is associated with a higher risk of death in HCC patients, 3) NAFLD may be an independent prognostic factor for HCC recurrence and survival, and 4) NAFLD has a negative impact on the outcome of patients undergoing liver resection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, non-invasive method of measuring the degree of liver steatosis.
the development of a novel, efficient and green method for the synthesis of some new 2-aryl-4, 6-diphenyl-4H-1, 3, 5-thiadiazine-2-ones.
the effects of the dietary intake of fructose, sucrose, and glucose on the risk of NAFLD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
steatosis is a risk factor for the development of liver fibrosis in hemochromato-sis, but not in HFE C282Y homozygotes with normal iron stores.
there is no clear evidence of an association between NAFLD and the development of liver cancer.
the use of the term “non-alcoholic fatty liver disease” (NAFLD) is not justified in the absence of liver injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of steatosis is a significant risk factor for the development of cirrhosis in hemochromatosisis.
the liver is an important site for iron storage and homeostasis.
the presence of steatosis is a major risk element for liver fibrosis and injury in hemochchromatosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is the major organ that is affected by the presence of excess iron in the body.

we have identified a new mechanism of liver injury in hemachromatosis, namely that the iron overload itself is not sufficient to cause liver disease, but rather, that iron overload is a cofactor for the development of steatosis, which then causes liver injury.
the gut microbiota can be manipulated to prevent and treat liver disease.
